\chapter{Complexity — NTIME}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NTIME
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module defines acceptance and deciding for finite nondeterministic multi-tape
Turing machines over the binary alphabet, where a branch accepts when it has halted
with output exactly the one-bit string $1$, and introduces the nondeterministic time
classes $\mathrm{NTIME}(T)$ of languages decided in time $c \cdot T$ for some constant
$c$ (Arora--Barak, Definition~2.5). It proves that acceptance and $\mathrm{NTIME}$ are
monotone in the time bound, that $\mathrm{DTIME}(T) \subseteq \mathrm{NTIME}(T)$, and
that $\mathrm{NTIME}(T)$ is empty when $T$ vanishes at some input length.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Nondeterministic acceptance within $t$ steps]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet with
finitely many states and two transition functions, one for each choice bit; let $x$ be
a binary string and $t \in \mathbb{N}$. We say that $N$ \emph{accepts $x$ within $t$
steps} if there is a choice word $w \in \{0,1\}^t$ such that running $N$ from its
initial configuration on input $x$ for $t$ steps, using the $i$-th bit of $w$ to select
the transition function at step $i$, reaches a halted configuration whose output is
exactly the one-bit string $1$. A branch halted with any other output, including the
empty string and $0$, is not accepting.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of acceptance in the branch length]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine over the binary
alphabet, let $x$ be a binary string, and let $t \le t'$ be natural numbers. If some
choice word of length $t$ drives $N$ on input $x$ to a halted configuration with output
exactly $1$, then some choice word of length $t'$ does as well; that is, if $N$ accepts
$x$ within $t$ steps then $N$ accepts $x$ within $t'$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Nondeterministically deciding a language in time $T$]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInTime}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine over the binary
alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let
$T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. We say that $N$ \emph{decides $L$ within time $T$} if
for every binary input $x$: every choice word of length $T(|x|)$ drives $N$ from its
initial configuration on $x$ to a halted configuration, and $x \in L$ if and only if
some choice word of length $T(|x|)$ drives $N$ on $x$ to a halted configuration with
output exactly the one-bit string $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The nondeterministic time class $\mathrm{NTIME}(T)$]
\lean{Complexity.NTIME}
\label{Complexity.NTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInTime}
For a time bound $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the class $\mathrm{NTIME}(T)$
consists of all languages $L$ of binary strings for which there exist a constant
$c \in \mathbb{N}$ and a finite nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine $N$ over the
binary alphabet such that, on every input $x$, every choice word of length
$c \cdot T(|x|)$ drives $N$ to a halted configuration, and $x \in L$ exactly when some
choice word of that length drives $N$ to a halted configuration with output $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of $\mathrm{NTIME}$ in the time bound]
\lean{Complexity.NTIME.mono}
\label{Complexity.NTIME.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin.mono, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{5}
Let $T_1, T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be time bounds with $T_1(n) \le T_2(n)$ for
every $n$. Then $\mathrm{NTIME}(T_1) \subseteq \mathrm{NTIME}(T_2)$: every language of
binary strings decided by some finite nondeterministic multi-tape machine within
$c \cdot T_1(n)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, for some constant $c$, is also decided
by such a machine within $c \cdot T_2(n)$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic time is contained in nondeterministic time]
\lean{Complexity.DTIME_subset_NTIME}
\label{Complexity.DTIME_subset_NTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.NTIME, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{4}
For every time bound $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$,
$\mathrm{DTIME}(T) \subseteq \mathrm{NTIME}(T)$. That is, if a language $L$ of binary
strings is decided by a finite deterministic multi-tape Turing machine that, for some
constant $c$, halts on every input $x$ within $c \cdot T(|x|)$ steps with output $1$ if
$x \in L$ and $0$ otherwise, then $L$ is decided by a finite nondeterministic
multi-tape machine within $c \cdot T(|x|)$ steps on every input $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing time bounds give the empty class]
\lean{Complexity.NTIME_eq_empty_of_exists_zero}
\label{Complexity.NTIME_eq_empty_of_exists_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a time bound with $T(n) = 0$ for at least one
input length $n$. Then $\mathrm{NTIME}(T) = \emptyset$: no language of binary strings
is decided by a finite nondeterministic multi-tape machine within $c \cdot T(|x|)$
steps on every input $x$, for any constant $c$.
\end{theorem}
